audit_findings.title: Convertible-note dilution is inconsistent with an interest-burdened equity numerator
audit_findings.magnitude: Approximately 19.47m gross conversion shares, or 15.4% of the 126.755295m denominator; removing them as a sensitivity, not as the final correction, raises bear/base/bull value per share from $45.42/$63.26/$70.60 to approximately $53.66/$74.74/$83.41.
audit_findings.mechanism: The gross conversion shares inflate the denominator even though OE retains interest expense, conversion requires cash settlement of at least $700m principal, and capped calls offset some conversion value above principal.
audit_findings.evidence: However, upon conversion of any Convertible Notes, the conversion value, which will be determined over a period of 40 trading days, will be paid in cash up to at least the principal amount of the Convertible Notes being converted.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated claim-consistency error. Gross conversion shares materially depress every per-share result, but the correct adjustment is smaller than simply removing all 19.47m shares because residual dilution can arise above the conversion and capped-call prices.
audit_findings.action: Recalculate net incremental shares using the $700m principal, 27.8178-share conversion rate, cash-principal settlement formula, approximately $49.34 capped-call price, and counterparty-performance terms; then rerun all per-share scenarios with interest expense retained.

audit_findings.title: The post-year-end Utica acquisition breaks the valuation perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: $464.6m cash consideration, equal to 81.9% of the $567.3m anchor; filed post-closing results through 2026-06-30 were $16.7m revenue and $9.3m operating income; net OE effect unquantified.
audit_findings.mechanism: The OE anchor excludes the acquired operations, while post-transaction financing and share claims enter the valuation through interest expense, debt context, and the denominator.
audit_findings.evidence: Subsequent to December 31, 2025, in February 2026, the Company completed its acquisition of certain upstream and midstream assets in the state of Ohio from Antero Resources Corporation and certain affiliated entities (collectively, “Antero”), effective as of July 1, 2025 (together, the “Utica Acquisition”).
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter mismatch of a scale reasonably capable of changing value. The omitted acquired cash generation raises value, while acquisition financing, sustaining capital, taxes, and other recurring costs reduce it, so the net direction cannot be established from the supplied partial-period figures.
audit_findings.action: Construct a pro forma Utica OE schedule covering operating cash flow, settled hedges, cash taxes, sustaining capital, incremental interest, and transaction-related shares from the closing date; align the anchor, denominator, and balance-sheet date before rerunning the valuation.

audit_findings.title: The latest-actual anchor may capitalize an exceptional hedge gain indefinitely
audit_findings.magnitude: $201.3m 2025 settled-derivative gain, equal to 35.5% of the $567.3m anchor; 2026 first-half settled derivatives reversed to a $104.0m loss.
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained in anchor OE and grown into perpetuity, a temporary hedge receipt increases every forecast year and terminal value rather than running off with the underlying contracts.
audit_findings.evidence: For 2025, we realized a gain on settled commodity derivatives of $201.3 million, compared to a $83.2 million gain in 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The hedge gain and subsequent reversal are demonstrated, but its exact inclusion in the OE workpaper remains unresolved. Its size and reversal make indefinite capitalization reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion; removing the 2025 gain dollar-for-dollar would reduce the base buy-below sensitivity to about $28.67 versus the $25.92 price before considering a proper hedge-runoff schedule.
audit_findings.action: Trace settled derivatives through the 2025 OE calculation and replace any indefinitely capitalized amount with contract-by-contract runoff or a normalized commodity-price and hedge-cycle schedule; rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: A one-time legal recovery appears capable of inflating anchor OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $48.6m net cash recovery, equal to 8.6% of the $567.3m anchor; a full dollar-for-dollar removal sensitivity lowers base value to approximately $57.87 per share and buy-below to approximately $40.51, still well above the $25.92 price.
audit_findings.mechanism: If included, the nonrecurring $81.7m settlement revenue less $33.1m legal expense raises anchor OE and is propagated through forecast growth and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company received a net cash settlement of $ 48.6 million after deducting approximately $ 33.1 million in legal settlement expenses.
audit_findings.explanation: Inclusion in the anchor is unresolved and should be corrected if present. Nevertheless, even the conservative sensitivity of removing the entire filed net recovery does not approach changing the stated buy conclusion; it leaves approximately $14.59 per share, or 56%, between buy-below and market price.
audit_findings.action: Trace both settlement revenue and legal expense through OE, remove them together with applicable cash-tax effects if included, and document the normalization even though the isolated adjustment is not conclusion-changing.

audit_findings.title: Share-settled SAR dilution is acknowledged but absent from the denominator
audit_findings.mechanism: Shares issued to settle the existing SAR dollar payout would increase the fully diluted denominator; retaining SBC expense does not capture that already-granted share claim.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company plans to settle the SARs Awards that were granted in 2023 with shares.
audit_findings.explanation: The planned share settlement and denominator omission are demonstrated, but the filing does not provide the payout or resulting share count. The record therefore establishes possible overvaluation but cannot establish whether the dilution is material.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the 2023 SAR award quantities, market-cap appreciation thresholds, performance-period terms, payout caps, and settlement-price convention; calculate net shares at 2026-09-06 and rerun per-share values without adding back SBC expense.

audit_findings.title: Future plugging obligations may be omitted after accretion is added back
audit_findings.magnitude: $54.949m filed noncurrent ARO at 2026-06-30 and $53.727m total ARO at 2025-12-31; deducting $54.949m lowers base value by approximately $0.43 per share and buy-below by approximately $0.30 per share.
audit_findings.mechanism: If accretion is added back while plugging cash outlays are absent from sustaining capital, the obligation is missing from OE; alternatively, it can be recognized once in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company has asset retirement obligations associated with the future plugging and abandonment of proved properties and related facilities.
audit_findings.explanation: Coverage in sustaining capital remains unresolved, but the recorded obligation is only about 0.7% of the $8.018bn base equity value. Even deducting the entire filed noncurrent balance separately leaves the buy conclusion unchanged by a wide margin.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile historical and forecast plugging payments to sustaining capital and the ARO roll-forward; if they are excluded from OE, deduct the complete current and noncurrent ARO once in the bridge and confirm there is no double counting.
